title: A small garden-notes experiment
purpose: Explain a simple way to record observations while keeping causal conclusions qualified.
constraints: Preserve the distinction between an observed pattern and an established cause.

sources.text: A weekly garden note records what was planted, the watering schedule, and the conditions observed. Comparing these notes can help a gardener notice patterns, but a single week's result does not prove what caused a plant to grow.

claims.statement: A garden notebook may help a person notice patterns; the notes alone do not establish a cause.

review.reason: The illustrative brief preserves the sample source purpose and its causal qualification.

requested_outputs.description: Draft one concise introductory post using the source and retaining its causal qualification.
